headline: Salt Lake sings in four-part harmony and screams in all-ages basements.
summary: Salt Lake music runs on two engines. One is institutional: the Tabernacle Choir, the Utah Symphony and clean-cut pop from the Osmonds to Neon Trees. The other is a stubborn DIY underground of all-ages rooms like Kilby Court, KRCL community radio and SLUG Magazine. That scene's flyer and poster language can give the gray City Edition a voice.

insights.title: The name is the story nobody tells
insights.detail: The Jazz were named in New Orleans and moved to Utah in 1979, so the franchise carries a genre name with no local jazz roots. Utah has a real if small jazz scene. The link is mostly typographic and nostalgic, not sonic. The name sits in a market that rarely sings about it.
insights.implication: Pair a local jazz-and-improv voice with product, so the name is earned rather than ironic. A New Orleans-to-Wasatch story could anchor a capsule.

insights.title: Credibility is earned in all-ages rooms
insights.detail: Utah's alcohol laws and young population made all-ages rooms like Kilby Court in the Granary District the proving ground for generations of bands. Gig posters, screen-printed flyers and SLUG Magazine culture set the visual language.
insights.implication: Screen-print and flyer looks read as real here, and a polished stadium-rock look would not. Use them for tees and hoodies.

insights.title: Choir culture shapes how the city hears harmony
insights.detail: The Tabernacle Choir, the Utah Symphony at Abravanel Hall, and ward and stake music mean many locals grew up singing in parts. The anthem and group singalongs land with unusual unity in an arena.
insights.implication: Leave sacred and church imagery alone. Build on celebratory, communal sound instead, such as crowd-sung moments and sound-wave graphics.

insights.title: Hometown exports give the market swagger
insights.detail: Imagine Dragons formed in Provo and Las Vegas with BYU roots. Neon Trees came out of Provo, and the Osmonds out of Ogden defined an earlier era. A Provo-to-Orem emo and pop-punk lineage runs beside them. Utah claims these acts as its own even when they live elsewhere.
insights.implication: Artist collaborations need licensing and likely run through management. The safer route is crediting local-scene lineage in editorial content, with no logos or lyrics.

insights.title: The West Side holds the rhythm
insights.detail: Rose Park and Glendale are home to Mexican-American and Pacific Islander communities, with their own church choirs, quinceanera and family-party music, and lowrider and cumbia culture. You hear it at community gatherings far more than at downtown venues.
insights.implication: Work through community partners and pay local creators. Never lift Polynesian motifs without a collaborator.

insights.title: A young roster meets a young audience
insights.detail: Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey play beside Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. The team's story is youth and development, which mirrors Utah's youngest-in-the-nation demographic and its music-making teenagers.
insights.implication: Build drops around emerging local artists, not legacy acts, to rhyme with the rebuild.

places.name: Kilby Court
places.why: A tiny backyard-style all-ages room that launched many Utah indie bands. It is the emotional center of the DIY scene.

places.name: The Depot
places.why: A converted historic rail depot and a mid-size room for touring and national acts.

places.name: Urban Lounge
places.why: A long-running indie and punk club east of downtown.

places.name: The Complex
places.why: A multi-room venue for hip-hop, EDM and touring shows.

places.name: Metro Music Hall
places.why: A mid-size club for touring acts and local showcases.

places.name: Abravanel Hall
places.why: Home of the Utah Symphony. The city's institutional musical heart, a short walk from the Delta Center.

places.name: KRCL 90.9 FM
places.why: Independent community station that champions local artists and world music.

places.name: Graywhale and Randy's Records
places.why: Long-standing local record shops where the scene crate-digs.

places.name: Delta Center
places.why: The Jazz home and the largest concert room in the state. Game nights are the most reliable mass-music moment.

places.name: Sugar House
places.why: A bar, record and vintage corridor with a younger, creative crowd.

people.name: Imagine Dragons
people.why: Utah-rooted arena act with BYU and Provo origins. A source of Utah pride, but any collaboration means national-level licensing.

people.name: Neon Trees
people.why: Provo band with a national hit run and a Utah scene touchstone.

people.name: The Osmonds
people.why: Ogden-linked family that defined Utah's earlier pop moment.

people.name: Utah Symphony
people.why: Institutional anchor, with a summer home at Deer Valley in Park City.

people.name: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square
people.why: The state's best-known musical institution. Treat it as sacred and avoid commercial imagery.

people.name: SLUG Magazine
people.why: Salt Lake Under Ground has documented the DIY scene for decades, and its poster art is a design cue.

people.name: KRCL DJs and programmers
people.why: Community-radio voices who lift local and world music.

moments.name: Utah Arts Festival
moments.why: The state's biggest multi-day arts and music festival, at Library Square, with a poster-art tradition.

moments.name: Home opener and NBA Cup Nuggets night
moments.why: An early Friday-night spotlight for a local artist performance and drop.

moments.name: Home games at Delta Center
moments.why: In-arena music, DJs and halftime culture make this the most scalable local music stage.

moments.name: Salt Lake Pride
moments.why: A major community and music weekend downtown.

moments.name: Deer Valley Music Festival
moments.why: The Utah Symphony's summer season in Park City.

moments.name: Red Butte Garden summer concerts
moments.why: A long-running outdoor concert series at the foot of the Wasatch.

vocabulary.meaning: The urban strip along the mountains from Provo to Ogden, and the scene's geography.
Warehouse neighborhood that houses Kilby Court and creative spaces.
Local congregation structures and many musicians' first stage. Use the terms respectfully.
The local default for DIY shows, given age-restricted bar culture.

designCues.use: Accent on tees and tape, echoing a clear winter-inversion sky.
Base of capsule graphics, with print-fade treatments.
Limited colors, off-register ink and hand-lettered date blocks on tees.
Hang tags, packaging and woven labels.

designCues.cue: Sound-wave contours that echo the Wasatch skyline

designCues.use: Use sparingly, as a contrast to the cool City Edition palette.

productHooks: Gig-poster tee series, one design per month of home games, made with local screen printers and poster artists.
Hang tags and packaging styled as 7-inch sleeves, with a local artist playlist QR.
A New Orleans-to-Wasatch jazz capsule that ties the name to a real local jazz voice.
Gray-to-blue gradient warm-up jacket with a sound-wave contour liner.
watchouts: Never use Tabernacle Choir, temple or other church imagery or music commercially.
Artist names and recordings (Imagine Dragons, Neon Trees, the Osmonds) require licensing. Never use lyrics.
Pacific Islander and Latino cultural motifs come only through paid community collaborators. Never lift them.
Alcohol-forward venue imagery is a poor fit for Utah's youth-heavy, family audience.
